name: Old God
summary: Across Azeroth, the Old Gods’ whispers still poison mortal minds and twist the world. Once they ruled the primordial world, until the Titans bound them beneath the earth. Their influence endures.

sections.title: Masters of the Primordial World
sections.body: In Azeroth’s first age, the Old Gods ruled through vast bodies of chaotic flesh, among them C'Thun. They took root in the planet’s crust and commanded elemental armies and insectoid swarms. When the Titans arrived, their armies waged an apocalyptic war against the Old Gods. Rather than destroy them, the Titans bound them in vast prisons beneath the earth.

sections.title: Whispers from the Deep
sections.body:
The Old Gods have never truly slept beneath their chains, miles of stone and enchanted wards. Their psychic malice seeps into the world and corrupts the vulnerable. During the War of the Ancients, that malice slowly drove Neltharion the Earth-Warder mad and twisted the noble dragon into Deathwing.

As the Great Sundering’s raging waters swallowed Queen Azshara and her Highborne, an Old God answered their desperation. The Old God transformed them into the serpentine naga.

sections.title: Stirrings in the Sands
sections.body:
Many mortal civilizations now treat the Old Gods as myth, though their prisons are fracturing. Nearly a millennium ago, insectoid qiraji swarmed from southern Silithus in the War of the Shifting Sands. They served C'Thun until the night elves and dragons sealed them behind the Scarab Wall.

Today, cults such as the Twilight's Hammer gather in dark corners across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Their foul rites seek to break the Titans’ bindings and hasten the end of all mortal life.

faq.q: What exactly are the Old Gods?
faq.answer: The Old Gods are ancient, eldritch monstrosities of flesh and madness who ruled Azeroth in primordial times. They feed on chaos and seek to corrupt the world, driving mortals and elementals toward madness.

faq.q: How many Old Gods were there on Azeroth?
faq.answer: No mortal knows for certain how many Old Gods there were. C'Thun, imprisoned beneath Ahn'Qiraj in Silithus, is best known. Others lie chained in subterranean vaults across the globe.

faq.q: Why didn't the Titans just kill them all?
aliases: why didn't titans kill old gods
faq.answer: The Old Gods had burrowed so deeply into Azeroth’s bedrock that tearing them out risked destroying the world. So the Titans built prisons instead.

faq.q: Are the Old Gods connected to Deathwing and the naga?
faq.answer: Yes. The Old Gods whispered into Neltharion the Earth-Warder’s mind and slowly drove him mad, until he snapped and became Deathwing. As the Great Sundering’s waters raged, an Old God answered Queen Azshara and her Highborne’s cries. It remade them into the naga.

The Twilight's Hammer is an apocalyptic cult devoted to nihilism and the Old Gods. Its followers seek to unbind the imprisoned entities, unleash the elemental lords and plunge the world into total ruin.

faq.q: Where are the Old Gods imprisoned?
faq.answer: The Old Gods’ known prisons lie scattered across the world, deep beneath Titan ruins. C'Thun is trapped beneath Ahn'Qiraj in Silithus. Others were bound beneath the northern reaches and deep subterranean foundations.

angles.text: As a kaldorei, you fought the qiraji minion hordes in the War of the Shifting Sands and sealed Silithus behind the Scarab Wall.
As a priest who delves into shadow magic, you walk a perilous path. Beware the maddening whispers said to rise from ancient horrors chained beneath the earth.
As a druid, you hold a sacred duty to guard the Emerald Dream against the Emerald Nightmare. Its true source remains unknown.
As a warlock, you draw mainly on fel magic and demons of the Burning Legion. Some foolishly seek the forbidden curses and sacrificial rites left behind by the Old Gods’ servants.
